headline: Old sync server retired, TrooVault costing app demoed, and a security review of the data platform

items.title: Old sync server retired
items.detail: Every data pipeline (Unicommerce, Shopify, ClickPost, Meta, Gmail reports, Ozonetel and the dbt models) has run on ECS Fargate for 3 weeks without the old server, so the server itself is now removed: the machine, its fixed IP address, its access role, 5 stored keys and 2 alarms, 35 items in all. A full backup of its disk is kept until February 2027. All pipelines were checked before and after, and kept running normally.

explain.simple:
We used to run all our data jobs on one always-on computer in AWS. Over the last few weeks every job moved to a newer setup that only starts a machine when a job needs to run.

The old computer was switched off three weeks ago and nothing needed it, so now it is removed completely. That brings the monthly AWS bill down by about 6%, and there is one less machine to look after and keep secure. A backup copy is kept for a few months, just in case.
explain.technical: Terraform removal of module "uniware_sync" (EC2 instance, Elastic IP, security group, IAM role + instance profile), the 4 deploy-key modules, 6 role policies attached to that role and 2 CloudWatch alarms: plan 0 add / 1 change / 35 destroy. The one change drops the box's two IPs from the RDS security group; office, Metabase and Fargate rules unchanged. EBS snapshot kept outside the module (delete ~2027-02). Verified after apply: instance terminated, role gone, Uniware/dbt/ClickPost/Ozonetel runs all SUCCESS. Saving: about $8.6 a month (disk, public IP, 5 secrets, 2 alarms) of a ~$135 monthly usage bill (Cost Explorer, before credits and tax).

items.title: Access cleanup: Google Sheets and GitHub
items.detail: Read access to the reference Google Sheets is now limited to exactly the two pipelines that use them, and 7 old GitHub access keys that only the retired server used were removed from 6 repositories. Sheets sync and every pipeline keep running as before.

explain.simple: Fewer doors left open: only the two jobs that actually read our Google Sheets can still read them, and old keys that let the retired server download our code are deleted.
explain.technical: prod-gcp: Workload Identity attribute condition and service-account bindings now list only the uniware-sync and troovy-analytics Fargate task roles (plan afterwards: no changes). GitHub: all read-only deploy keys deleted; 0 deploy keys left across the 9 org repositories.

items.title: TrooVault costing app: first version built and demoed to the COO
items.detail: The costing app now has a name, TrooVault, and its first full version was demoed on 13 Nov. It has a login for each role (founders, NPD category managers, procurement, tech), a weekly raw and packing material buy list with cost, products taken from our active Shopify listings, and a drag-and-drop board for assigning categories. Recipes are locked with a key per category, so each NPD manager sees only their own category's recipes. There is also a built-in team chat (one-on-one and groups), an activity log, and an in-app guide for every role.

explain.simple: One app where the team enters product recipes and immediately sees the cost and margin of each pack. Recipes are our most private data, so they are locked: founders see everything, each category manager sees only their own category, and procurement sees only the total quantities it has to buy each week.
explain.technical: Next.js + Postgres. Role-based access with a View-as toggle for founders and tech. Recipe encryption happens in the browser: a personal key per user and category keys handed out with a key-code check, plus a recovery kit; the server stores only sealed recipes and RM/PM totals, so costing runs on the totals without the recipe in clear text. Team chat with sent/delivered/seen ticks, a typing indicator and an unread badge; recipe groups are locked with the category key. Every change is written to the audit log. Products come from the active Shopify listings in the production DB, read-only.

items.title: Security review of the data platform
items.detail: Reviewed the AWS account, the database and all pipelines for security. This added account activity logging and automatic threat detection, with alerts going to the same email as pipeline failures, turned on two-step login for the admin account, and removed an unused network rule. The database checks (encryption, backups, secure connections only) all passed.

explain.simple: A check of how well our data is protected. Every action in our AWS account is now recorded, and AWS watches for anything suspicious and emails us if it sees something. The database was already encrypted and backed up.
explain.technical: CloudTrail multi-region trail (1-year S3 retention) and GuardDuty (RDS login, S3 and Lambda protection) via Terraform, with findings of severity 4 or higher sent to the pipeline-alerts SNS topic through EventBridge. MFA on the IAM admin user; an unused security group deleted. RDS checked: encrypted, deletion protection, 7-day backups, SSL forced, scram-sha-256.

items.title: Customer complaints month on month (new card)
items.detail: A new Metabase card with complaints per 1,000 orders, refund rate, the top 3 complaint reasons and CSAT for each month. Complaint data starts on 1 Aug 2026, so the card covers August onwards.

explain.simple: One row per month showing how many orders led to a complaint, how many were refunded, and what customers complained about most.
explain.technical: Card 240: KwikEngage tickets assigned to an agent with a complaint tag, against Shopify orders and refunds per IST month; top 3 reasons by tag; CSAT from the ratings table.

items.title: XpressBees vs Delhivery month to date, by warehouse
items.detail: A query comparing the two couriers this month for each warehouse: orders, delivered, RTO % and NDR %.

explain.simple: A quick side-by-side of our two main couriers for each warehouse this month.
explain.technical: reporting.ops_report_orders, orders created this month (IST), cancelled excluded; RTO % = RTO / (delivered + RTO); one row per facility and courier.

items.title: Meta ads cards open on this month
items.detail: The two Meta ads cards now show the current month by default.

explain.simple: The Meta ads numbers open on this month straight away, without picking dates.
explain.technical: Cards 230 and 231: date filter default changed to This month.

items.title: Health check of all data pipelines
items.detail: Checked the last 10 days of all 11 data pipelines: every one is running on schedule. The few failed runs were short outages on the Google or Unicommerce side that the next run picked up on its own, plus the COGS sheet sync that was already fixed on 8 Nov.

explain.simple: A routine check that all our data is still arriving on time. It is, and nothing was missed.
explain.technical: ops.*_runs for all 11 pipelines: last run and last success today for each; Uniware 4 failed runs out of ~61k (Google Sheets / Unicommerce 503s, connection reset), each followed by a successful run; staging_core failures only 3-8 Nov (COGS sheet), 0 since.

items.title: Ozonetel call data now flowing
items.detail: Ozonetel's team connected their call system to our receiver for the inbound line, and call records now arrive automatically: about 1,280 calls were in the database by 14 Nov.

explain.simple: Every customer call on the inbound line now shows up in our data by itself, a few minutes after the call.
explain.technical: Ozonetel callback to our Lambda receiver, files in S3, loader every 15 min into raw.ozonetel_calls; 1,284 calls by 14 Nov, 0 loader errors.

items.title: Docs updated for the new setup
items.detail: The infrastructure and Meta pipeline docs now describe the Fargate setup only, with the right rollback steps.

explain.simple: The written instructions now match how things actually run today.
explain.technical: Infrastructure docs and Terraform comments, meta-sync docs and README: EC2 rollback removed, rollback = previous image tag + apply.

upcoming.title: Costing web app, first version
upcoming.detail: BOM entry, cost per pack and margin views for the 6 roles, with an Excel upload for the first load.

explain.simple: The first usable version of the costing app: teams enter product recipes and see the cost and margin of each pack.
explain.technical: v0 scope: BOM entry, cost-per-pack and margin views for 6 roles, Excel bulk import for the first load.

upcoming.title: First real Ozonetel calls in the data
upcoming.detail: Check the first calls against the Ozonetel dashboard, then add calls next to chats in the customer complaints dashboard.

explain.simple: Once calls start arriving, we check they match Ozonetel's own screen, then show calls and chats together in one complaints view.
explain.technical: Verify raw.ozonetel_calls vs the Ozonetel dashboard, enable the no-callback alarm, rotate the callback token, add a calls block to the complaints card.

upcoming.title: Demand projection model: new logic
upcoming.detail: Reworking the projection model: base daily rate from a 30/60-day blend, per-channel growth, and checking the safety-stock Z-score against past months.

explain.simple: Improving how the forecast works out expected sales, so plans are closer to what actually sells.
explain.technical: Base daily rate from a 30/60-day blend, per-channel growth, and a backtest of the safety-stock Z-score against past months.

upcoming.title: Demand dashboard: lost sales, forecast accuracy, KPI tiles
upcoming.detail: The next cards on the planning dashboard after Plan vs Stock.

explain.simple: New cards that show sales missed because of stock-outs, how close past forecasts were, and headline numbers at a glance.
explain.technical: Next Metabase cards on dashboard 12: lost-sales estimate, forecast vs actual accuracy, KPI tiles.
